answer.evidence: The main body is a set of vertical bamboo stalks (rows 7-27) with node lines every 7 rows (rows 12, 13, 19, 20, 26, 27). They are drawn as vertical faces with no horizontal top surface, ellipse, or front-edge line with eave shadow. The leafy band at rows 2-6 is a canopy texture seen face-on, not a sloped plane over an edge line. The base at rows 28-31 is a grass strip. The object reads as a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bamboo trunk band of vertical green stalks with dark green separators. It has 14 distinct colours and a median of 13 per tile, against 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references, so it is far below both. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green and counts as dark material tone, as in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas. Shading is shallow: each stalk has about 3 green steps (light, mid, dark) and a few node ticks. It has no per-leaf clumps or grain like the reference canopies and trunks. The piece is thin and sparse, so I do not fail it on the density number alone. By eye it still looks flatter and more uniform than the references, with simple repeated vertical stripes and little highlight work. A careful artist would not accept it next to them without it looking thinner and flatter.
